script: I thought my love was safe—until I read these twisted comments.. I last posted a variation of this a little over 5 years ago. We're a little overdue for a repost. Everyone's all "A+++ would ride again" with Uber, eBay, Amazon. But /r/relationship_advice comments are the opposite. Like, every problem post turns into a magnet for "break up with them" and "get rid of them" tea. Two things to keep front of mind when you're posting: 1. Most folks here are stuck on a challenge they can't solve solo. 2. Those challenges are usually either impossible or super hard to manage. So you're telling your story, and the commenters bring their own grudges. Result? Every post gets drenched in "end it" comments. The number of solid "maybe stay" replies shows if ending is actually worth it. Let me break it down with my Uber analogy: If the red flag is bleeding—every comment says run. Zero stars on our inverted scale. Relationship cooked. Cheated once? Most say run because "once a cheater, always a cheater." Maybe one or two say stay. One or two stars. Spouse got drunk, made out, apologized, no history? Some still say leave, but enough say stay. Two or three stars. Good relationship but they forget your love language? Advice on communication pops up, but some still say leave. Three to four stars. Everything's rosy and you're asking for celebration ideas? A few trolls want a breakup, but the rest say it's fine. Four to five stars. Same logic for platonic or work relationships. Basically, the "leave" comments outnumber the "other" ones by a lot because people remember drama. If everyone says break up, probably do it. If a quarter say something else, give that 25% a shot. TL;DR: Most comments urge you to end things because people are drama‑hungry or have a bleak view of love. The more "other" advice you get, the more worth it is to try it. (Thanks to u/NotAmericanDontCare for sparking this repost. Comments open a bit, but keep it civil, besties.)
